key_insight: TrackEverything rethinks point tracking by modeling a video as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates, rather than as isolated 2D frame-to-frame motion. This lets the tracker handle dense points over long horizons without the usual short-clip limitation.
problem_solved: Existing point tracking methods force a tradeoff between tracking a few query points over long time spans and tracking many/all points only over short video clips. This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon dense tracking in videos.
method: Represent the video as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates instead of only 2D image-space correspondences.
De-duplicate track information so the model does not need to repeatedly process the same scene content across long durations.
Decouple model complexity from video length, enabling scalability to longer sequences while maintaining dense tracking coverage.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could make dense tracking more practical for long videos, improving applications in robotics, AR/VR, scene understanding, and video analysis. It also suggests a new design pattern: use 3D persistent scene representations to overcome temporal scaling limits in 2D tracking.

paper_title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
paper_authors: Ayush Jain, Sreeharsha Paruchuri, Ishita Gupta, Fan Zhang, Tanner Schmidt
